content_units: - Your budget is currently running at about   118% of take-home pay  , so the main goal is to trim flexible categories first rather than cut essentials aggressively.
Biggest Overspending Areas and Revised Budget

Using a practical “not extreme” approach, the top three categories to target are   dining out, shopping, and groceries  . These are the largest flexible expenses and offer the cleanest savings without disrupting fixed obligations.
Category   Current   Reasonable Cut   Revised Budget   Notes
Dining out   $540   $220   $320   Still allows about 1–2 meals out per week
Shopping   $410   $160   $250   Keeps room for clothing/household extras
Groceries   $620   $120   $500   Achievable with meal planning and fewer convenience buys
Subscriptions   $96   $36   $60   Trim unused or overlapping services
Miscellaneous   $260   $60   $200   Add a cap for unplanned spending
Travel sinking fund   $300   $100   $200   Keeps travel savings, just slower
Phone   $85   $15   $70   Possible via plan review/autopay discount
Gym   $70   $10   $60   Only if a cheaper plan exists
That brings spending from   $4,941   down to about   $4,220/month  .
- High for one monthly budget unless you are supporting others, buying premium items, or relying on delivery/prepared food.
- This is the strongest cut opportunity.
- Usually the easiest discretionary category to cap.
This version aims to be realistic while nearly balancing the month.

That would put you at about   $4,170–$4,200  , which is much safer.
To estimate “overspending,” I treated   rent, insurance, student loan, utilities, and most transport   as harder-to-change fixed costs, and focused mainly on categories with the most flexibility.
